sources.name: ALMA Science Archive (Titan, giant planets, Pluto)
sources.description: Archive of ALMA submillimetre interferometry data. Solar-system programs include Titan molecular maps and Io; the archive holds raw measurement sets and calibrated products.

sources.name: CICLOPS - Cassini Imaging Central Laboratory for Operations
sources.description: Official Cassini ISS imaging team site with image releases and map products of Saturn, rings and moons. PDS holds the full archive.

sources.name: Titan topography models (Corlies et al. 2017, Cornell eCommons)
sources.description: ISIS cube files of Titan topographic models combining Cassini RADAR altimetry, SARtopo and stereo-derived DTMs, with a global interpolation. Useful for georeferencing or draping Titan radar data on heights.
sources.notes: License stated as CC0 1.0 in the record

sources.name: ESA Juice mission (cruise, Earth-Moon flyby imagery)
sources.description: Mission page for ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, en route to Jupiter. Cruise cameras and the JANUS science camera imaged the Moon and Earth in the August 2024 lunar-Earth flyby and again at the 28 September 2026 Earth flyby (740 JANUS images according to DLR). ESA says data will be released through the PSA.

sources.name: ESA Planetary Science Archive (PSA)
sources.description: Official archive of ESA planetary missions (Mars Express, Rosetta, Venus Express, SMART-1, Giotto, Huygens, ExoMars TGO, BepiColombo, Juice, Hera), mostly in PDS4. The web interface searches by mission, instrument, target and time, and downloads need no login.

sources.name: ESA PSA: Huygens DISR (HP-SSA-DISR)
sources.description: ESA PSA volume with Huygens Descent Imager/Spectral Radiometer raw and calibrated data (v1.3), browse PNGs, and extras by E. Karkoschka including descent mosaics and movies.

sources.name: ESO Science Archive Facility (SPHERE, VLT)
sources.description: ESO archive of VLT and other data; includes SPHERE adaptive-optics images of Io, Titan and giant planets. Public after a proprietary period; some downloads require free registration.

sources.name: JAXA Hisaki (SPRINT-A) EUV observations of Jupiter and Io
sources.description: Earth-orbiting EUV spectroscopic telescope observing the Io plasma torus and Jupiter's aurora. Data are distributed through JAXA's DARTS archive; its Hisaki catalog layout was not verified here.

sources.name: New Horizons image gallery (JHUAPL)
sources.provider: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
sources.description: Mission team's gallery of processed New Horizons images of Pluto, Charon, Jupiter and Arrokoth. Browse-quality processed images, not the raw archive (see PDS SBN).

sources.name: JunoCam raw images and citizen-science processing
sources.provider: Southwest Research Institute / NASA JPL (Mission Juno)
sources.description: Public site where raw JunoCam image data can be downloaded and processed by anyone, with citizen-scientist products shown alongside. Covers Jupiter's cloud tops and poles and the close flybys of Ganymede, Europa and Io.

sources.name: JUPOS - Jupiter Observations Project
sources.description: Community project measuring and cataloging features on amateur images of Jupiter and Saturn, with data sets, drift charts and software linked to image collections.

sources.name: Keck Observatory Archive (KOA)
sources.provider: NASA Exoplanet Science Institute (IPAC) / W. M. Keck Observatory
sources.description: Archive of Keck I/II data including NIRC2 adaptive-optics imaging and OSIRIS/HIRES/LRIS/DEIMOS/MOSFIRE; widely used for Io, Titan, Neptune, Uranus and asteroid imaging. Proprietary periods apply, with public data free to download.

sources.name: MAST: HST and JWST archive (solar system programs)
sources.description: Primary archive for HST and JWST data, with solar-system observations of the giant planets, rings, Titan, Pluto/Charon and Galilean moons. Search by target name; proprietary data are released after the exclusive-access period.

sources.name: OPAL - Outer Planet Atmospheres Legacy (HST HLSP)
sources.description: High-level science products from the Hubble OPAL program: yearly global maps of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune in WFC3 filters, calibrated and map-projected. Available as FITS and downloadable through MAST.

sources.name: Cassini VIMS Data Portal (Nantes)
sources.provider: Laboratoire de Planetologie et Geosciences, Nantes Universite
sources.description: University of Nantes portal presenting Cassini VIMS spectral cubes of Titan and the icy moons with multispectral previews, cube download, and Titan global infrared mosaics (Le Mouelic et al. 2019). Site returns HTTP 403 to scripted requests, so it was confirmed from search results, not loaded.

sources.name: Dragonfly mission (Titan rotorcraft)
sources.description: Mission site for Dragonfly, NASA's Titan rotorcraft lander. No flight data yet; landing-site work relies on Cassini RADAR, VIMS and Huygens DISR data listed in this catalog.
sources.notes: No data yet; included as the Titan reference mission

sources.name: NASA Europa Clipper mission (cruise and Mars flyby data)
sources.description: Mission page for Europa Clipper (launched October 2024). In the Mars flyby of 28 February 2025 E-THEMIS took over 1000 thermal infrared images and cameras imaged Phobos and Deimos; releases are on the NASA Photojournal. PDS archive status of cruise data was not confirmed.

sources.name: NASA Planetary Photojournal (Jupiter gallery)
sources.description: JPL's catalog of released planetary images with PIA identifiers, captions and links to source products; has target galleries for Jupiter and the other outer planets. Processed releases, not raw data.

sources.name: Callisto Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Callisto with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: Enceladus Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Enceladus with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: Europa Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Europa with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: Ganymede Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Ganymede with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: Io Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Io with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: Mimas Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Mimas with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: Titan Trek
sources.description: NASA's web-based Trek portal for exploring Titan with layered mission mosaics and maps in an interactive viewer. The page is a JavaScript application; its layer list was not enumerated here.

sources.name: NRAO Data Archive (VLA, VLBA, GBT)
sources.description: Archive of VLA, VLBA, GBT and ALMA-NA data including radio maps of Jupiter's radiation belts, planetary thermal emission and asteroids. Browse, search and download calibrated products from the NRAO archive (login only for proprietary data).

sources.name: NSSDCA Pioneer 10/11 project and data sets
sources.description: NSSDCA project page for Pioneer 10 (Jupiter 1973) and Pioneer 11 (Jupiter 1974, Saturn 1979), linking each spacecraft's experiments and data sets. Follow the per-spacecraft data set pages for imaging photopolarimeter products; the page itself mostly lists fields-and-particles data.

sources.name: PDS Atmospheres Node: Cassini archive
sources.description: Cassini mission archive page at the Atmospheres Node, the entry to Cassini data sets curated by this node, with documentation.

sources.name: Huygens probe data (PDS Atmospheres)
sources.description: Directory of the Huygens probe archive hosted at NMSU, including the DISR (Descent Imager/Spectral Radiometer) volume hpdisr_0001. DISR imaged Titan's surface during the 14 January 2005 descent.

sources.name: Juno atmospheres data overview (PDS Atmospheres)
sources.description: Overview of Juno data sets held by the Atmospheres Node, including JIRAM, UVS and the Microwave Radiometer (MWR), which sounds Jupiter's deep atmosphere at several microwave frequencies.

sources.name: Juno JIRAM data (PDS Atmospheres)
sources.description: Juno Jovian Infrared Auroral Mapper (JIRAM) imager and spectrometer data of Jupiter's atmosphere, aurora and the Galilean moons, from the PDS Atmospheres Node.

sources.name: Juno UVS data (PDS Atmospheres)
sources.description: Juno Ultraviolet Spectrograph (UVS) data: far-UV spectral images of Jupiter's aurora and atmosphere, plus Galilean moon observations.

sources.name: PDS Atmospheres Node (ATM)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Atmospheres Node (New Mexico State University)
sources.description: PDS node for planetary atmospheric data: Mars weather and MSL REMS, Venus, giant planet and Titan atmosphere, occultation and spectral data. Mostly non-image time series, but includes some atmospheric image products such as Mars dust and cloud observations.

sources.name: PDS Imaging Node: Cassini mission page
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Imaging Node entry page for Cassini ISS, VIMS and RADAR, linking the PDS Image Atlas product search, online data volumes and documentation. Best starting point for Titan SAR, ISS and VIMS products.

sources.name: Cassini ISS (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Cassini Imaging Science Subsystem raw EDR and calibrated images of Saturn, its rings and moons, plus the Jupiter flyby. Narrow- and wide-angle cameras. Cassini data is also searchable by target in OPUS.

sources.name: Cassini RADAR (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Cassini RADAR SAR swaths, altimetry and radiometry of Titan's surface through the haze, including BIDR map-projected products. Primary source for Titan lakes, dunes and mountains.

sources.name: Cassini VIMS volumes (PDS Imaging)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Online data volumes of Cassini VIMS spectral cubes (visible and infrared channels) of Saturn, Titan and the icy moons, as raw and calibrated cubes in PDS3 format with browse images.

sources.name: PDS Imaging Node: Galileo mission page
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Imaging Node page for Galileo SSI image data (REDRs) and NIMS spectral data (EDRs and cubes) with Image Atlas search and documentation. Primary source for Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto close-ups.

sources.name: PDS Imaging Node: Juno mission page
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Imaging Node page for Juno JunoCam and Stellar Reference Unit data, with Image Atlas search, online volumes and documents.

sources.name: PDS Imaging Node: Voyager mission page
sources.provider: NASA PDS Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node (JPL / USGS)
sources.description: Imaging Node page for Voyager 1 and 2 ISS images with Image Atlas search, online volumes and documentation. Covers all four giant planets and many moons.

sources.name: Cassini CIRS data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Cassini Composite Infrared Spectrometer data: thermal infrared spectra and focal-plane maps of Saturn, Titan, icy moons and rings. Free download; PDS3 labels with data tables or images.

sources.name: Cassini ISS data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Cassini Imaging Science Subsystem narrow- and wide-angle camera images of Saturn, its rings and moons (including Titan), 2004-2017, as raw and calibrated products with browse images. Free download; PDS3 labels with data tables or images.

sources.name: Cassini UVIS data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Cassini Ultraviolet Imaging Spectrograph data: UV spectral images of Saturn, rings, Titan and Enceladus plumes, plus stellar and solar occultations. Free download; PDS3 labels with data tables or images.

sources.name: Cassini VIMS data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Cassini Visual and Infrared Mapping Spectrometer image cubes (0.35-5.1 micrometres) of Saturn, rings and moons, distributed from the Rings node with ring/moon observation geometry. Free download; PDS3 labels with data tables or images.

sources.name: Galileo Jovian ring data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Galileo observations of Jupiter's rings and small inner moons held at the Rings Node, with accompanying documentation.

sources.name: HST ring-moon data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Hubble Space Telescope observations of outer planets, rings and moons re-archived by the Rings Node with PDS labels and geometry metadata.

sources.name: New Horizons data (PDS Rings Node mirror)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Rings Node copy of released New Horizons LORRI and MVIC data (Jupiter, Pluto system, Arrokoth), also indexed in OPUS. The authoritative archive is the PDS Small Bodies Node.

sources.name: PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: NASA PDS node for ring and moon data of the giant planets. Holds Voyager, Galileo, Cassini (ISS, VIMS, UVIS, CIRS), New Horizons and HST ring/moon products, browsable by mission volume with raw and calibrated data. Searchable by observation geometry through OPUS.

sources.name: OPUS - Outer Planets Unified Search
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Search tool that finds Voyager, Galileo, Cassini, New Horizons and HST observations of the outer planets by target, time, ring/moon geometry, wavelength and instrument. Returns browse previews and links to the underlying PDS product files; also has a documented REST API.

sources.name: Voyager ISS data (PDS Rings Node)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Ring-Moon Systems Node (SETI Institute)
sources.description: Voyager 1 and 2 Imaging Science Subsystem images of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, their rings and moons, with geometry metadata and browse previews. Includes the Uranus (1986) and Neptune/Triton (1989) encounter images.

sources.name: New Horizons data at the PDS Small Bodies Node
sources.description: Authoritative PDS archive of New Horizons data: LORRI, MVIC and LEISA (Ralph), Alice and other instruments for the Jupiter flyby, Pluto system, Arrokoth and the extended mission. PDS4 bundles with raw, calibrated and derived products.

sources.name: Arrokoth surface composition maps (PDS SBN)
sources.description: Derived Arrokoth surface composition maps from LEISA and MVIC spectral data of the 2019 encounter, in the PDS4 nh_derived bundle.

sources.name: Arrokoth geology and geophysical maps (PDS SBN)
sources.description: Derived LORRI/MVIC products for Arrokoth: geology and geophysical maps from the 2019 encounter. A PDS4 successor in the nh_derived bundle includes shape-model products.

sources.name: New Horizons LORRI Jupiter encounter (PDS SBN)
sources.description: Directory of the PDS3 LORRI Jupiter encounter data set (frames from the 2007 flyby), including images of Jupiter, Io volcanic plumes and the Galilean moons.
sources.notes: PDS3 volume; PDS4 equivalents exist as nh_lorri:jupiter_raw / jupiter_cal

sources.name: New Horizons LORRI KEM1 raw (PDS SBN)
sources.description: LORRI raw images from the first Kuiper Belt Extended Mission, including the 2019 Arrokoth encounter and distant Kuiper Belt object observations. The raw KEM1 data have been reissued in several versions, so check for the current one.

sources.name: Pluto albedo maps (PDS SBN)
sources.description: Derived Pluto albedo maps from New Horizons imaging, delivered in the nh_derived PDS4 bundle.

sources.name: Pluto system derived geophysics products (PDS SBN)
sources.description: Derived New Horizons Pluto-system geophysics data in the nh_derived PDS4 bundle; sibling collections hold albedo, composition and atmospheric products from the 2015 flyby.

sources.name: PVOL2 - Planetary Virtual Observatory & Laboratory
sources.provider: Universidad del Pais Vasco (UPV/EHU) Planetary Sciences Group
sources.description: Database of amateur and professional planetary images of Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, Venus, Uranus and Neptune with thousands of contributor observations since 2005, searchable by date, filter and observer. Open browsing; uploads need registration.

sources.name: SMOKA - Subaru-Mitaka-Okayama-Kiso Archive
sources.description: NAOJ's archive for Subaru Telescope (Hyper Suprime-Cam, FOCAS, MOIRCS, IRCS, COMICS), plus Okayama, Kiso and Mitaka telescopes. Search by coordinates or name; public data after the proprietary period, with registration needed for download of some items.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Ariel Voyager Image Control Network
sources.description: Voyager 2 control network for Ariel using most usable mission images; basis for Voyager-era Ariel cartography. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: outer solar system maps (browse by target)
sources.description: Astropedia catalog of cartographic products, mosaics, DEMs, control networks and nomenclature for planetary bodies; use the target filter for moons of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune and for Pluto/Charon. Covers Mimas, Phoebe and Uranian-moon products not listed individually here.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Callisto Galileo-Voyager Global Mosaic 1 km
sources.description: Global Callisto image mosaic assembled from Galileo SSI and Voyager images at about 1 km/px. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Charon New Horizons LORRI-MVIC Global DEM 300 m
sources.description: Stereo-derived digital elevation model of Charon from New Horizons at 300 m/px. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Charon New Horizons LORRI-MVIC Global Mosaic 300 m
sources.description: Charon mosaic from New Horizons LORRI and MVIC images at 300 m/px. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Dione Cassini-Voyager Global Mosaic 154 m
sources.description: Global Dione mosaic from Cassini ISS with Voyager images filling gaps, simple cylindrical projection at 64 pixels per degree. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Enceladus Cassini ISS Global Mosaic HPF 110 m
sources.description: Global Enceladus mosaic from 586 Cassini ISS images (CLR, GRN, UV3, IR3) with a high-pass-filtered version, shifted to match IAU longitudes. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Europa Voyager-Galileo SSI Global Mosaic 500 m
sources.description: Global Europa image mosaic from Voyager and Galileo SSI at 500 m/px, the standard basemap for Europa studies. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Ganymede Voyager-Galileo SSI Global Mosaic 1 km
sources.description: Global Ganymede image mosaic combining Voyager and Galileo SSI data at 1 km/px. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature
sources.description: IAU-approved feature names for planets and satellites, with coordinates, diameters and approval dates, searchable by body; helps locate named features on Titan, Io, Pluto and others.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Iapetus Cassini-Voyager Global Mosaic 803 m
sources.description: Global Iapetus mosaic from Cassini flyby images with Voyager filling the poles. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Io Galileo SSI/Voyager Color Merged Global Mosaic 1 km
sources.description: Io global mosaic combining Galileo SSI color ratios with high-resolution monochrome base maps; color data are 1.3-21 km/px, monochrome 1-10 km/px. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Io Voyager-Galileo SSI Global Mosaic 1 km
sources.description: Global Io mosaic where Galileo SSI is supplemented with Voyager 1 images for the poorly seen subjovian hemisphere (63 MB GeoTIFF). Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Jupiter Voyager and Galileo Global Mosaics
sources.description: Collection page for Jupiter-system global mosaics built from Voyager and Galileo imaging. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: New Horizons Global Mosaics
sources.description: Collection page for the Pluto and Charon global mosaics and elevation products from New Horizons. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Oberon Voyager Image Control Network
sources.description: Voyager 2 control network that, per its description, also includes the southern hemispheres of Titania and Umbriel. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Pluto New Horizons LORRI-MVIC Global DEM 300 m
sources.description: Stereo-derived digital elevation model of Pluto's best-imaged hemisphere (about 591 MB), in equirectangular and cube forms. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Pluto New Horizons LORRI-MVIC Global Mosaic 300 m
sources.description: Pluto mosaic from LORRI and MVIC images (about 296 MB) covering the hemisphere seen at best resolution. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Rhea Cassini-Voyager Global Mosaic 417 m
sources.description: Rhea global mosaic built mostly from Cassini images, with a few Voyager images filling north polar gaps. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Saturn Voyager Airbrush Global Products
sources.description: Early airbrushed global cartographic products of Saturn's moons made from Voyager images in support of Cassini planning. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Tethys Cassini Global Mosaic 293 m
sources.description: Global Tethys image mosaic from Cassini ISS at 293 m/px. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Initial Global Control Network and Mosaicking of ISS Images of Titan
sources.description: Geodetic control network and mosaicking products for Cassini ISS images of Titan, the basis for the USGS ISS global mosaics. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Titan Cassini ISS Global Mosaic 4005 m
sources.description: 2015 global map of Titan made from Cassini ISS images through flyby T100 (about 7.8 MB GeoTIFF). Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Titan Cassini ISS Near Global Mosaic 450 m
sources.description: Higher-resolution Cassini ISS mosaic of Titan covering all longitudes between roughly +45 and -65 latitude; the file is large (about 1.5 GB). Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Titan Cassini SAR-HiSAR Global Mosaic 351 m
sources.description: Preliminary global radar mosaic combining Cassini SAR and high-altitude SAR swaths through flyby T104. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.

sources.name: USGS Astropedia: Triton Voyager 2 Global Color Mosaic 600 m
sources.description: Global color mosaic of Triton from Voyager 2 images (1989) at 600 m/px; only part of the moon was imaged at good resolution. Public domain; download from the Astropedia product page.
